info.title: Coloplus Remote Monitoring API

parameters.description: Only those whose next action is overdue
parameters.name: overdue

get.description: Received files only. Coloplus's internal files are left out for Airtel. For acceptance, owner_id is the site's id.
get.summary: Files on a ticket, incident, dispute or acceptance

post.description: Step 1 of 3. Say what the file is and what it belongs to; the answer is a short-lived link. Step 2: PUT the file to that link with exactly the headers given. Step 3: POST /attachments/{id}/complete. Accepted: JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF, plain text, CSV, Word and Excel files, up to the size limit, at most 25 per ticket, incident, dispute or acceptance. The file goes straight to private storage and is checked against the SHA-256 you give. A file is only visible once confirmed. 503 when file storage is not set up.
post.summary: Ask for a link to upload one file

post.description: Step 3 of 3. Checks the stored file is the size and SHA-256 declared; if not it is discarded and you start again. Repeating it is safe. Only the sender can confirm.

get.description: Checks you may see the file and returns a link that works for a couple of minutes and makes the browser save it, never display it. Every link issued is recorded in the audit log. Open the link at once; do not store it.
get.summary: A link to read one file

get.description: Newest first. Needs audit access, which is separate from editing rights. A reader scoped to some sites sees only events about those sites.

post.description: Always answers the same way, whether or not the address has an account, so it cannot be used to find out who does. The link works once and expires in an hour.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset link

post.description: Checks the password and, when two-step verification is on, the authenticator code. On success the access token is set as an HttpOnly cookie and also returned. When a code is needed the response status is "mfa_required" and no token is issued: send the request again with totp_code.

get.summary: The signed-in user, their permissions and site scope

post.description: Returns ten one-time recovery codes. They are shown this once; only their hashes are kept. People whose role needs two-step verification can do nothing else until this succeeds.
post.summary: Confirm a code and turn on two-step verification

post.description: Needs a current authenticator code. The old codes stop working at once. The new ones are shown this once.
Returns a secret and an otpauth:// link to show as a QR code. Two-step verification turns on only after /auth/mfa/enable confirms a code.
The token comes from the emailed link and works once. Choosing a password signs out every earlier session.
post.summary: Choose a password with an invitation or reset link

parameters.description: draft, submitted, approved, rejected or superseded
parameters.name: status

get.description: Airtel users receive the published view of approved reports only.
get.summary: One report with its calculated summary

put.description: Replaces the notes and intervals. Send the row_version you loaded; if someone else changed the report meanwhile you get a conflict. Saving a returned report makes it a draft again.

post.description: The approver cannot be the author. Approving a correction supersedes the report it corrects.
post.summary: Approve and publish a submitted report

post.description: Creates a new draft revision linked to the approved one. The approved report is untouched until the correction is approved by someone other than its author.
post.summary: Start a correction of an approved report
Return a submitted report to its author

post.description: Safe to repeat: submitting an already submitted report changes nothing. A report submitted after its site would already show "Awaiting update" (the day ended more than the site's freshness window ago) needs late_reason; without it the answer is 400 saying so. A correction does not.

parameters.description: Why it is late, when it is
parameters.name: body

get.description: Today's status, a trailing 7-day health strip, pooled 30-day availability and open-incident count, one card per assigned site. A site with no approved report in the window has a null availability -- never 0 -- and every bar red.

Availability pools active sites by eligible minutes over the period. A day with no approved report counts its window as unknown; it never appears as available. Give `date` for one day, or `from` and `to` (at most 92 days). `region` narrows the sites; `regions` lists what is on offer. Each site row says how many of the days were reported and, when its report is current, the source it was last observed running on.
get.summary: Portfolio overview for a day or a period

parameters.description: One reporting day, defaults to today (Africa/Lagos)
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: First day of a period; give with to
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Last day of a period (not in the future)
parameters.name: to

get.description: One point per reporting day for the active sites in scope, pooled by eligible minutes. A day on which nothing was reported has null availability: draw a gap, not a line at zero or 100. Daily is the finest grain the reports give.

parameters.description: Last day (not in the future); at most 92 days
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: open, under_review, awaiting_evidence, agreed_correction, resolved or closed
parameters.name: status

get.summary: Headline dispute counts for your scope

get.description: Both parties' comments and every status change, oldest first. Coloplus's internal notes and staff details are left out for Airtel.

post.description: Both parties can comment. Coloplus can mark a comment internal so Airtel never sees it. An Airtel comment on a dispute waiting for their evidence hands it back to Coloplus.

Coloplus: open to under_review, then awaiting_evidence, agreed_correction or resolved. Resolving needs an outcome; upheld needs the correction agreed first and, for a report, the corrected approved revision. Airtel: closed withdraws it, or acknowledges a resolution; under_review gives evidence or reopens a resolution. Repeating a step that already happened changes nothing. Coloplus's approval and Airtel's agreement are recorded separately.
post.summary: Move a dispute to its next status

get.description: One row per site and reporting day, approved reports only. A day without an approved report is still a row, marked no_approved_report with no served or outage figures, never zero and never available. Every row carries the report revision, basis, coverage, formula and version, dispute state, time zone, units (minutes and percent), generation time and assumptions. Needs export access; an export is recorded in the audit log.

parameters.description: Last day (not in the future); at most 92 days
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: One site; default every site in scope
parameters.name: site_id

get.description: One row per reported fault that started in the period, with its site, severity, impact, status and observed times. Airtel gets published incidents only, as everywhere else. Duration is blank until restoration is recorded; a restoration target is a plan and is shown apart. Faults with no outage are told apart by impact. Needs export access; an export is recorded in the audit log.
get.summary: Export the incident register as CSV

parameters.description: Last day (not in the future); at most 92 days
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: One site; default every site in scope
parameters.name: site_id

post.description: The entry stays in the record with the reason and no longer counts. Repeating it changes nothing.

get.summary: List incident corrections in your scope

post.description: Writes the corrected value to the incident and the decision to the correction, in one transaction. Never the person who requested it. Refused once the incident is closed.

get.description: Airtel users see only incidents that have been published to them.

parameters.description: Only incidents owned by this person
parameters.name: owner_id

parameters.description: reported, acknowledged, assigned, in_progress, restored, verified or closed
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Only incidents whose promised update is overdue
parameters.name: overdue

get.summary: Open, active, critical and overdue incident counts

get.description: Staff get the full record and every update. Airtel gets the published view and the updates written for them.

post.description: The owner must be an active person who can work on incidents at that site. Assigning a reported or acknowledged incident moves it to assigned. Optionally set the next action and when the next update is due.

Corrects when a fault started or when it was actually restored. The current value is snapshotted server-side, never taken from the request. Refused once the incident is closed. Only one request per incident and field may be awaiting review at a time; that answers 409.
post.summary: Ask to correct an incident field

post.description: Does not wait for the daily report to be approved, so a critical incident can be notified at once. Safe to repeat.

Stages run reported, acknowledged, assigned, in_progress, restored, verified, closed. Restoration needs the time power was actually restored; a target does not count. Verification needs a new observation (what and when) from someone other than the person who recorded restoration. Closing needs a root cause. Repeating a step that already happened changes nothing.
post.summary: Move an incident to its next stage

post.description: Anyone who can work on the incident may add a note. Supervisors can also set the plan (next action, next update time, restoration target) and mark an update for Airtel, which needs the incident to be published first.
post.summary: Add an update to an incident

get.description: Failed emails stay here until someone retries them. The message text is never returned.

parameters.description: Search Airtel code, Coloplus code or name
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Installed power source: grid, generator, battery, solar or building_supply
parameters.name: source

get.summary: A site's acceptance with its history

post.description: Only for a site still pending acceptance, and only once per site.
post.summary: Start a site's commissioning and acceptance

post.description: Coloplus: requested to built, then ready_for_inspection with the dossier; a rejected site goes back to built once fixed. Airtel: ready_for_inspection to inspected or rejected; inspected to accepted or rejected. Either side can put it on_hold with a reason and resume it by naming the stage it left. Only Airtel's accepted counts as acceptance, and it brings a pending site into service. Repeating a step changes nothing.
post.summary: Move a site's acceptance to its next stage

post.description: Creates a draft for a site and reporting day. Intervals must stay within the day (Africa/Lagos), be whole minutes, and not end in the future. A served interval names its source; an outage has none. Served and outage intervals may not overlap.

Disputes a site, a period, a published report, or one interval of it. Only an approved report can be disputed. The same thing cannot be disputed twice while the first dispute is open; that answers 409.

get.description: The estimate is labelled as one and says how it was reached. With no agreed rate, or nothing recorded, available is false and reason says why; there is never a made-up number. Notes and who recorded an entry are for Coloplus only.
get.summary: A site's fuel: estimated level and entries

post.description: delivery adds litres to the tank ("1,000 litres delivered"). reading says what the tank held when someone looked and replaces the estimate. The estimate is then worked out from the site's agreed litres per hour and the generator hours reported each day. Send client_key and retry safely.
post.summary: Record a fuel delivery or a tank reading

post.description: Records a fault. Use impact no_outage for a fault that interrupted nothing, so it stays apart from service interruptions. The start time is when the fault began; the detection time defaults to it.
post.summary: Report an incident at a site

get.description: Profile, current condition and as-of time, the last days (gaps included, never shown as zero or available), open incidents, open disputes and the acceptance process. Sections the caller may not see are left out; Airtel gets published incidents only.
get.summary: The whole site screen in one call

parameters.description: How many reporting days to show (default 14, max 90)
parameters.name: days

post.description: Asks Coloplus for help with a site: a fault, a refill, an access problem. The priority is the one you ask for; Coloplus decides the severity of any incident it opens. Send client_key and retry safely: the same key returns the same ticket. Attachments are not supported yet.

get.summary: Headline ticket counts for your scope

get.description: Both sides' comments and every status change, oldest first. Coloplus's internal notes and staff details are left out for Airtel, and so is a linked incident until it is published to them.

post.description: Both sides can comment, also after it is resolved. Coloplus can mark a comment internal so Airtel never sees it.
The incident must be at the same site. The link is noted internally; Airtel sees it on the ticket only once the incident has been published to them.
post.summary: Link a ticket to the incident opened for it (Coloplus)

post.description: Coloplus: open to in_progress or resolved, in_progress to resolved, and resolved back to in_progress. Resolving needs a note. Airtel: status open reopens a resolved ticket, with a note. Repeating a step that already happened changes nothing.
post.summary: Move a ticket to its next status

post.description: Leave the password out and the person is emailed a link to choose their own.

patch.description: Only the fields present are changed. site_ids replaces the whole assignment list.

post.description: For someone who has not chosen a password yet. The earlier link stops working.

For someone who lost both their phone and their recovery codes. Turns it off, deletes their recovery codes, signs them out everywhere and emails them; they set it up again at their next sign-in. You cannot reset your own.

decided_at.description: DecidedAt is when Airtel accepted. Nothing else counts as acceptance.

dossier.description: Dossier is what Coloplus submitted when it declared the site ready.

held_from.description: HeldFrom is the stage a hold returns to.

ready_age_hours.description:
ReadyAgeHours is how long the site has waited for inspection since it
was declared ready. It is not operational performance.

waiting_on.description: WaitingOn is coloplus or airtel: whose move it is.

party.description: Party is who sent it: airtel or coloplus.

status.description: Status is pending until the upload is confirmed, then ready.

generator_hours.description: GeneratorHours is required only when PowerStatus is "outage", 0-24.

power_status.description:
PowerStatus, when set, is the reporter's simplified day-level entry:
"served" (power on all day) or "outage" (had an outage). It builds the
day's single interval and Intervals is ignored.

password.description:
Password is optional. Leave it out and the person is emailed a link to
choose their own.

color.description:
Color is green (reported, no outage), amber (reported, had an outage)
or red (no approved report that day -- a visible gap).

internal.description: Internal keeps the comment inside Coloplus; Airtel never sees it.

description.description: Description is what Airtel wrote when raising it.

outcome.description: Outcome is upheld or not_upheld once Coloplus resolves it, withdrawn if Airtel dropped it.

resolved_at.description: ResolvedAt is Coloplus's decision; AcknowledgedAt is Airtel's agreement.

waiting_on.description: WaitingOn is whose move it is: coloplus or airtel; empty once closed.

internal.description: Internal and AuthorID are only ever sent to Coloplus staff.

open.description: Open is every dispute not yet closed.

with_coloplus.description: WithColoplus are waiting on Coloplus; WithAirtel on Airtel (evidence or acknowledgement).

url.description: URL works for a couple of minutes and makes the browser save the file.

error.example: we couldn't find what you were looking for

anchor_kind.description: The estimate starts from the latest reading, or the first delivery.

basis.description:
Basis is always "estimate": the level comes from what people entered and
the agreed litres per hour.

consumption_lph.description: ConsumptionLPH is the agreed litres per running hour used.

hours_run.description: HoursRun and ConsumedLitres cover the reported days since then.

litres.description:
Litres is the estimated level. While UnreportedDays is above 0 it is the
most the tank could hold, because those days' use is unknown.

over_capacity.description: OverCapacity means the estimate exceeds the tank, so an entry is probably wrong.

reason.description: Reason says why there is no estimate, when there is none.

updates.description: Updates is the full history for staff; Airtel's updates are inside Published.

open.description: Open is every incident not yet closed; Active is those still awaiting restoration.

customer_visible.description: CustomerVisible shares this update with Airtel; the incident must be published.

next_action.description:
The plan fields are supervisor-only. A restoration target is a plan,
not a restoration.

basis.description: Basis is observed (default) or declared. Only observed counts.

source.description: Source is required when served and must be empty for an outage.

totp_code.description:
TOTPCode is the six-digit authenticator code, or a recovery code, needed
when two-step verification is on.

mfa_setup_required.description:
MFASetupRequired is true when the person is signed in but their role
needs two-step verification they have not set up: everything else is
refused until they have.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "mfa_required". With mfa_required no token is issued;
send the same request again with totp_code.

mfa_setup_required.description:
MFASetupRequired: the role needs two-step verification that is not on
yet, so permissions are empty until it is.

recovery_codes_left.description: RecoveryCodesLeft is how many unused recovery codes remain.

availability_pct_30d.description:
AvailabilityPct30d is the pooled reported availability over the
trailing 30 days. Null when the site has no approved report in the
window -- never 0.

bars.description: Bars is the trailing 7 days, oldest first (last entry is today).

today_status.description:
TodayStatus is the report that best represents today's live status
(in-progress if there is one, else approved); nil when nothing has
ever been filed today.

date.description: Date is the last day of the period, kept for clients that ask for one day.

from.description: From and To are the first and last reporting day pooled into the figures.

outages_this_week.description:
OutagesThisWeek counts distinct site/day pairs in the trailing 7 days
(inclusive of the requested date) whose current report has an outage.
An approximation, not a full weekly aggregation.

region.description:
Region is the filter applied, empty for every region; Regions lists the
regions in the caller's scope for the filter to offer.

category.description:
Category is incorrect_outage, missing_outage, incorrect_served,
wrong_duration, wrong_metric, missing_report or other.

interval_id.description: IntervalID narrows it to one interval of that report.

metric.description: Metric is availability, coverage, outage_minutes, served_minutes or other.

period_from.description: PeriodFrom and PeriodTo are dates (2026-12-01); give both or neither.

report_id.description:
ReportID is the published report being disputed; leave empty to dispute
the site or a period as a whole.

title.example: Outage shown on a day power was on

category.description:
Category is power_outage, low_fuel, generator_fault, equipment_fault,
access_restriction or other.

client_key.description:
ClientKey is optional. Send the same value when retrying a request that
may have gone through, and you get the same ticket back, not a second one.

contact_email.description:
ContactEmail is where Coloplus can reach the requester; it defaults to
your own address. Coloplus replies by email to your account, not to this.

priority.description: Priority is the priority you ask for: low, medium, high or critical.

client_key.description:
ClientKey is optional. Send the same value when retrying a request that
may have gone through, and you get the same entry back, not a second one.

kind.description:
Kind is delivery (litres added to the tank) or reading (litres the tank
held when someone looked, which replaces the estimate).

note.description: Note is for Coloplus only; the customer never sees it.

occurred_at.description: OccurredAt is when it happened (RFC 3339); it cannot be in the future.

late_reason.description: LateReason is why the report was submitted late; absent when it was on time.

open_disputes.description:
OpenDisputes counts the disputes about this report that have not closed.
A disputed figure keeps showing it.

category.description:
Category is grid_loss, building_supply_loss, generator_failure, low_fuel,
battery_failure, rectifier_fault, electrical_fault, access_restriction or other.

detected_at.description: DetectedAt is when it was noticed; defaults to StartedAt.

impact.description: Impact is outage for a service interruption, no_outage for a fault that caused none.

severity.description: Severity is critical, major or minor.

started_at.description: StartedAt is when the fault began, as best known.

title.example: Generator failed to start after grid loss

open_disputes.description:
OpenDisputes maps a report id to its number of unclosed disputes;
reports with none are left out.

filename.description: Filename is shown to people; it is never used as a path.

owner_id.description:
OwnerID is the id of that ticket, incident or dispute. For acceptance it
is the site's id: a site has one acceptance.

owner_type.description: OwnerType is ticket, incident, dispute or acceptance.

sha256.description:
SHA256 is the file's SHA-256 as 64 lower-case hex characters. The store
refuses an upload that does not match it.

shared.description:
Shared lets Airtel see a file Coloplus sends. Left out, a Coloplus file
is internal. Airtel's own files are always visible to Coloplus.

generator_hours.description: GeneratorHours is required only when PowerStatus is "outage", 0-24.

row_version.description:
RowVersion is the version this edit was based on. A stale one is
rejected with a conflict.

token.description: Token is the value of the link's token parameter (invitation or reset).

consumption_lph.description:
ConsumptionLPH is the generator's agreed fuel use in litres per running
hour; null until agreed. TankCapacityLitres is the tank size; null if unknown.

condition.description: Condition is available, outage_reported or awaiting_update.

days.description: Days runs newest first and includes days with no approved report.

condition.description: Condition is available, outage_reported or awaiting_update.

current_source.description:
CurrentSource is what the site was last observed running on; absent when
the report is stale, the last interval was an outage or none was observed.

days_reported.description: DaysReported of the response's Days have an approved report.

responsible_team.description: ResponsibleTeam is the team accountable for the site.

summary.description: Summary pools the period; absent when no day of it has an approved report.

today_status.description:
TodayStatus/YesterdayStatus are the report that best represents that
day's live status (in-progress if there is one, else the approved
one); nil when nothing has ever been filed. For the reporter's own
progress view, not the approved-only Summary/Condition above.

late_reason.example: Site had no network until Tuesday

coverage_pct.description: The percentages are null when not applicable or unavailable, never 0.

internal.description: Internal keeps the comment inside Coloplus; Airtel never sees it.

resolution.description: Resolution is how Coloplus resolved it.

status.description: Status is open, in_progress or resolved.

internal.description: Internal and AuthorID are only ever sent to Coloplus staff.

kind.description: Kind is comment, status or link (staff only).

critical_open.description: CriticalOpen are unresolved tickets whose requester asked for critical priority.

next_action.description: NextAction and DueAt set the plan after this step.

note.description:
Note is the dossier when declaring the site ready, the reason when
rejecting or holding, and what was fixed when rework follows a rejection.

stage.description:
Stage is built, ready_for_inspection, inspected, accepted, rejected or
on_hold. To resume from a hold, name the stage it left.

note.description:
Note explains the step. Needed to ask for evidence, agree a correction,
resolve, give evidence, reopen and withdraw.

outcome.description:
Outcome is upheld or not_upheld, required to resolve. Upheld needs the
correction to have been agreed first.

resolution_report_id.description:
ResolutionReportID is the corrected, approved report revision that
settles an upheld dispute about a report.

status.description:
Status is under_review, awaiting_evidence, agreed_correction, resolved
or closed. Coloplus reviews and settles; Airtel withdraws, gives
evidence or reopens (under_review), and acknowledges a resolution (closed).

at.description:
At is when power was actually restored (restored) or when the
confirming observation was made (verified).

note.description: Note is required to verify (what was observed) and to reopen.

status.description: Status is acknowledged, in_progress, restored, verified or closed.

note.description:
Note explains the step. Needed to resolve, to reopen, and to take a
resolved ticket back into work.

status.description:
Status is in_progress or resolved for Coloplus, open to reopen a
resolved ticket for Airtel.

invited.description: Invited is true until the person has chosen a password.
Invited is true until the person has chosen a password.
